disclosures.name: TestCaller
disclosures.reason: runtime-capability: symtab_test.go's assertion requires f.Entry() < pc -- the function's entry address always strictly precedes a call site's return address within it. go2cs has no addresses, only opaque per-call-site PC tokens (the deliberate model managed_impl.cs's header documents throughout); FuncForPC(pc) mints a *Func whose Entry() returns that SAME token, so Entry() == pc by construction and the < assertion can never hold. Inventing a value strictly less than the token (e.g. subtracting a constant) would satisfy the assert with a number that means nothing this host can stand behind -- the same class of laundering the ManagedPointerTokens/reflect pointer-identity disclosures already refuse. Falsifiable in the parts that matter: the same assertion also checks ok, Name()'s suffix, and the file/line range: if any of THOSE ever mismatch, the row is a real defect, not this disclosure -- only the Entry()>=pc arm is pinned. Measured 2026-09-02: ok=true, Name()=the correct qualified name, file/line correct, Entry()==pc exactly (e.g. 27==27) on every reported iteration.

disclosures.name: TestPinnerConstStringData
disclosures.reason: runtime-capability: the test's own comment states its subject -- 'const string data is not in span'. It asserts that unsafe.StringData of a string LITERAL reads runtime.isPinned == true before, during and after a Pinner.Pin/Unpin, which is true in Go because RODATA is not a heap span: spanOfHeap answers nil and the non-Go-pointer arm answers pinned. golib has no RODATA -- a literal's bytes are a heap byte[] (rooted for the process's life but movable) and unsafe.StringData returns an element reference into it -- so the truthful managed answer for that storage is 'a Go heap object, not pinned', and that is what the row reads on its FIRST assertion, before Pin is ever called. Answering true for storage nothing pinned would be fabrication (this class's anti-laundering clause). A truthful form exists in principle -- literal storage on the Pinned Object Heap plus a registry of literal-backed arrays so isPinned can recognise them -- and is REFUSED as one row's consumer paying a corpus-wide, unpriced allocation-policy change; that form is this entry's rejoin clause. Only the first-assertion arm is pinned: Pin and Unpin on that pointer must still not panic, so a regression in the non-Go-pointer no-op reads as a defect, not as this disclosure. Design and prediction: docs/phase4/DESIGN-runtime-pinner.md section 6.1.

disclosures.name: TestUserArenaLiveness/Free
disclosures.signature: expected arena-referenced object to be finalized
disclosures.reason: the test gives an arena object v a pointer to a heap object with a finalizer, drops v (`v = nil`), frees the arena (or, in /Finalizer, drops it), and then requires that finalizer to run, from inside the same still-running frame. Go's per-safepoint liveness maps drop v at its last use; the CLR reports the slots of a frame with exception handling (the converted defer's try/finally) live for the frame's whole lifetime, so v and everything it references stay rooted while the test is looking. The arena itself releases everything it allocated (arena_impl.cs, C2 C3 USER ARENAS). Measured on linux, Release, tiered off, as a one-axis A/B over the frame alone: the identical sequence (allocate smallPointerMix through UserArena.New, set its C to a fresh heap object, SetFinalizer on it, Free, runtime.GC() twice) run behind a RETURNED NoInlining call leaves v, v.C and the arena all collected (weak references dead), while inline in the test frame v and v.C stay alive even with the test's `x` and `v` explicitly cleared and v held past the clearing store. GolibTests' RuntimeUserArenaTests.AnObjectReachableOnlyFromTheArenaLivesUntilFree guards the arena half. The same class as runtime/debug's TestFreeOSMemory. RETIRES when the host reports frame liveness per safepoint, or the converter can end a local's lifetime at its last use.

disclosures.name: TestLineNumber
disclosures.reason: structural (census A2 D1b, OWNER RULING 2026-09-28 via COORD: disclose, no emission change). The test reads runtime.Caller's line for calls placed on DIFFERENT lines of ONE statement or one package var spec: composite-literal elements (compLit, arrayLit, sliceLit), map keys and values (mapLit), the operands of a multi-line sum (intLit) and the arguments of a multi-line call (l39, l40). InjectDebugCall's first check (export_debug_test.go:30-33) reads the locked M's procid, which no M records here, and refuses `missing tid`. That is the FIRST blocker and it is expressible; the protocol behind it is register-level ABI on Go machine code, which is the representational part. The pin stays at the first blocker on purpose: recording a procid would turn SIGTRAP into a signal delivered to a CLR thread with no Go handler, INFERRED to be host-fatal and NOT run. Scoped to linux because debug_test.go is `(amd64 || arm64 || loong64 || ppc64le) && linux && !race`. MEASURED on linux (P1, master 2ff42f7a16 plus the P1 disclosure seat, Release, tiered off, .NET 10.0.12, go1.24.13, the full runtime row of 10,883 verdicts). Windows and darwin are NOT read. RETIRES when the host can inject a call into a stopped goroutine; by design it cannot.

disclosures.name: TestTinyAlloc
disclosures.signature: no bytes allocated within the same 8-byte chunk
disclosures.reason: runtime-capability: the test makes sixteen `new(byte)` allocations and requires two of them to share an 8-byte chunk (`uintptr(p)&^7`), the observable of Go's TINY ALLOCATOR, which packs sub-16-byte pointer-free objects into one 16-byte block. Every `new(byte)` here is a distinct CLR object (a ж box) with an 8-byte sync-block header, an 8-byte method-table word and its field, so two live objects can never sit within 8 bytes of each other: the smallest gap this object model can produce exceeds the chunk the assertion asks for. That is the same object-layout argument as TestEmptySlice's 344 versus 320, one size down, and it is a floor of the object model rather than an unbuilt feature. One assertion, so the pin is the only text the row can print. MEASURED on linux (P1, master 2ff42f7a16 plus the P1 disclosure seat, Release, tiered off, .NET 10.0.12, go1.24.13, the full runtime row of 10,883 verdicts). Windows and darwin are NOT read. RETIRES if a one-byte Go allocation ever has a managed footprint smaller than the chunk; it cannot on the CLR.
